decision.text: Voice seat reuses the `fast` slot of the session row (s.fast / by_agent / awake / sleep unchanged); s.fast_seat records who sits there. Alternative: a third role slot — rejected, it would touch every pair-wide loop (room, sweep, sleep).

The voice assistant gets the item tool through Servex's door (mcp_url left default) with built-in tools off (sdk.tools []); session-fast had no door at all. Cost: the http tool list rides along; alternative (a restricted allow-list) not done.
decision.alt: mcp_url empty + a hand-made item server

log.msg: Sessions.js: SERVEX_SESSION_ASSISTANT=voice|fast (default fast), voice_say(), voice_brief(), reseat on flip, heard() drops its text; 6 new unit checks (21 pass). Worktree voice-wake (pool full).

findings.text: Deliverable 6's live proof was never run: `proof.mjs` is in the diff, but `task.jsonl` has no result line (no PASS/FAIL, no place count), and the session ended "without landing". Run `sessions-wake/proof.mjs` in the voice-wake worktree and log its JSON output before merging. The unit half does pass: `node Servex/agents/Sessions.test.mjs` gives 21 checks passed, run by this reviewer.

`say()` and `hold()` choose the message shape from `this.voice_seat()`, the process-wide switch, but `heard()` drops the reply only when `s.fast_seat === "voice"`, which is set per session (Sessions.js ~859/1005 vs ~1240). If an agent from the old seat is still awake when the switch flips, it gets the voice-shaped prompt and its reply is still posted as chat. Using one test for all three would be simpler.

The voice spec leaves out `mcp_url: ""`, so the agent loads the whole Servex door (100+ tool schemas) next to `local.item`, on every per-sentence low-effort turn (Sessions.js ~1084). If it only needs `mcp__local__item`, an `allowed_tools` list or `mcp_url: ""` would keep it as lean as session-fast was. This may need `local` to stay attached on its own, so check Agents.js ~1110.
`voice_seat(s)` is called with an argument at Sessions.js ~340 but is defined with none (~363). It is harmless, but it reads as though the switch were per session, and it is not.
`last_owner_text()` stays as a wrapper, and nothing in the diff calls it any more (Sessions.js ~360). Remove it unless something outside the fence uses it.

The first run printed FAIL only because proof.mjs counted the smart assistant's 3 chat answers as replies; fixed in 189d0ee1a (counts the voice-assistant agent only) and re-checked on the saved session file.

answer.reply: fixed: proof run, result logged above (PASS, 3 places, all re = owner at); proof.mjs check narrowed in 189d0ee1a

declined: the switch is read once from the environment at boot, so it can only change across a Servex restart, which ends every agent; wake() reseats a session whose fast_seat differs before any prompt is sent. heard() uses the per-session fast_seat on purpose: it is the seat that actually spawned.

declined: mcp_url "" also drops the in-process mcp__local__item server (Agents.js door(): no url returns early with no local tools), and allowed_tools only pre-approves, it does not narrow the tool list. A lean door needs an Agents.js change outside this fence; logged as a cost caveat in the decisions above.

log.msg: needs_restart: Servex/agents/Sessions.js is loaded at boot. Nothing changes until SERVEX_SESSION_ASSISTANT=voice is set in the environment Servex starts with and Servex is restarted; without it the default stays fast. Not restarted by this minion.
